title: Creamy Italian Sausage & Spaghetti Squash Bake
summary: A tomato-free, high-protein spaghetti squash casserole with mild poultry Italian sausage, roasted red peppers, spinach, Parmesan, and mozzarella.
sourceNote: A lighter baked-pasta-style dinner built around spaghetti squash and mild chicken or turkey Italian sausage, with roasted red pepper providing sweetness and acidity in place of tomato sauce. The version originally posted used roasted red pepper in the yogurt sauce. The cooked version replaced the roasted red peppers with about 3/4 cup pesto blended with the Greek yogurt and chicken broth. This is a substantial flavor and nutrition change, so the original nutrition estimate no longer reflects the prepared dish accurately; the final estimate should be recalculated from the pesto brand and amount used.

ingredients.item: mild Italian chicken or turkey sausage
ingredients.note: raw links or bulk sausage; remove casings if needed
finely diced; or use 1 large shallot
lightly crushed; optional if the sausage is already fennel-forward
divided, plus more to taste if needed

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Cut the spaghetti squash in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Brush the cut sides with 2 tsp olive oil and season with about 1/4 tsp of the kosher salt. Place cut-side down on a parchment-lined sheet pan and roast until the strands are tender but still have a little bite, about 35–45 minutes.

When the squash is cool enough to handle, scrape the flesh into strands with a fork. Transfer the strands to a colander and let them drain while you prepare the filling. Removing this extra moisture keeps the finished casserole from becoming watery.

While the squash roasts, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Remove the sausage from its casings if needed and brown it, breaking it into chunky crumbles. Add the diced onion or shallot and 3 cloves of the garlic. Cook until the sausage is cooked through and the onion is softened. Stir in 1 tsp Italian seasoning and the optional 1/2 tsp crushed fennel seed.

Blend the drained roasted red peppers with 3/4 cup Greek yogurt, 1/2 cup chicken broth, 1/4 cup Parmesan, the remaining 1 clove garlic, 1/2 tsp black pepper, and the remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt until smooth. The sauce should be roughly the consistency of a loose Alfredo sauce.

Reduce the skillet heat to low. Pour the roasted-red-pepper sauce into the sausage mixture and warm gently, stirring frequently. Do not let the sauce boil aggressively, which can cause the yogurt to split. Add the spinach and stir until wilted.

Lower the oven temperature to 400°F. Fold the drained spaghetti squash strands and 1/2 cup of the mozzarella into the sausage mixture. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed, keeping in mind that the sausage, Parmesan, and mozzarella all contribute salt.
Transfer the mixture to a lightly greased casserole dish and top with the remaining 1/2 cup mozzarella. Bake at 400°F until hot and bubbling, about 15–20 minutes.

If desired, broil for 1–2 minutes to brown the cheese, watching closely. Let the casserole stand for about 5 minutes before serving. Offer red pepper flakes at the table so each person can add heat individually.

actualChanges: Replaced the roasted red peppers in the sauce with about 3/4 cup pesto. Blended the pesto with the Greek yogurt and chicken broth to make the sauce.

verdict.familyReaction: Jason rated it 4.25/5, Judy 3.75/5, and Ella 4/5, for an overall average of 4.0/5. Jason said the flavor and texture were great. The main concern was that the pesto substitution likely increased the calories substantially compared with the original roasted-red-pepper version.
whatWorked: The creamy pesto sauce delivered strong flavor.
The finished texture was very good.
All three tasters rated it between 3.75 and 4.25, indicating broad agreement that the dish worked.
whatDidnt: The planned roasted-red-pepper sauce was abandoned after the blender leaked because the seal was missing.
Using about 3/4 cup pesto likely made the dish significantly higher in calories and fat than originally intended.
verdict.nextTime: Decide whether to keep the pesto version as the preferred recipe or retry the roasted-red-pepper sauce with the blender properly sealed. If using pesto again, record the brand and nutrition label so the recipe's per-serving nutrition can be recalculated accurately.
